newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end higher, nearby strength noted.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end higher, nearby strength noted.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed sharply higher with nearby contracts particularly strong, boosted by Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report and a strong expiration to the December contract.

"There was a lot of enthusiasm off the strong expiry of the December contract but the bottom line is that we had good marketings and light cattle average weights. I think that was the one-two punch," one dealer said.
Friday's USDA cattle report which put November marketings at 97 percent of a year ago, above the average estimate in a pre-report Reuter survey of analysts of 93.9 percent.

The report also put November placements higher than expected at 108 percent of a year ago. Floor sources noted a larger than normal proportion of placements in the lighter weight categories was constructive for nearby contracts.
December, which expired at 1200 CST, was boosted by late short covering by locals and the spot month touched a peak of 67.950 cents and settled up 0.805 cents at 67.425 cents.

Floor sources also noted that February became the front month at a discount to cash and sentiment that it was undervalued contributed to its strong performance. February closed 1.225 cent higher at 64.800 cents a lb.

As further evidence of light weights, USDA on Friday in its weekly U.S. Meat Production report estimated the average weight of cattle slaughtered under federal inspection last week at 1,168 lbs, slightly under 1,169 estimated the previous week but sharply lower than 1,200 lbs a year earlier.
Feeder cattle futures closed sharply higher, boosted by spillover buying from live cattle and technically-based buying, floor sources said.
"There were a lot of buy stops in 66.55 cents on the March feeders. It seemed to be technical type buying," one floor source said.
March feeder cattle futures closed 1.425 cent higher at 67.275 cents a lb. Other months closed 1.250 to 0.250 cent up.
Volume on feeder cattle was estimated at 2,327 lots while live cattle futures turnover was put at 15,870 lots.
